summary: Suspicious sign-ins from a Cloudvault VPS in Germany outside the account baseline (F1). Most sign-ins originate from Germany (F2). VPN appliance vpn-edge-01 runs vulnerable firmware listed in CISA KEV (F3). Sign-in path touches an exposed asset; partial chain signals exist but no confirmed abuse chain. Risk Gate verdict: escalate (confidence 0.51).

risk.rationale: F1 confirms suspicious sign-ins from a Cloudvault VPS (DE) outside the account baseline using valid credentials (T1078.004), and F3 confirms the VPN appliance vpn-edge-01 is running firmware with multiple CISA KEV vulnerabilities (T1133/T1190) — confirmed exposure. However, this is not a confirmed account takeover chain: the link between the VPN appliance and the sign-ins is not established (F2 that most sign-ins come from DE is only LIKELY, not CONFIRMED), and there is an active data-quality conflict (DQ vpn_session_order failing for appliance:vpn-edge-01) that makes session attribution unreliable. Signals are not explained away (not benign) and F1 is confirmed rather than weak (not monitor). Conflicting/insufficient evidence with confirmed exposure requires human review.
